redcap_row.comments_v2: Prompt ACLS PEA management: CPR started at 01:20 (18s after handoff), LMA placed at 01:31, 1st Epinephrine 1 mg IV given at 01:44, bilateral breath sounds confirmed at 03:24, 1st 2-min pulse check at 03:47 with minimal pause (<8s), 2nd Epinephrine 1 mg IV at 04:04, and ROSC achieved at 06:08.
redcap_row.feedback_narrative_v2: At 01:02, the team rapidly assigned roles (Compressor, Airway, Meds, Team Leader) and initiated chest compressions at 01:20. The Team Leader immediately recognized PEA as a non-shockable rhythm (01:24), prioritized airway placement (01:31) and Epinephrine 1 mg IV (administered at 01:44), and systematically verbalized H's and T's (hypoxia, PE/thrombus, hypovolemia/electrolyte derangement from diarrhea at 02:00-02:55). The Compressor proactively requested lung auscultation at 03:12 to confirm airway placement. Two-minute pulse checks were well-timed (03:47 and 06:00) with a second dose of Epinephrine at 04:04. Upon achieving ROSC at 06:08, the team appropriately ordered IV fluids, 12-lead ECG, chest X-ray, head CT, and specialist consultations. Areas for refinement include avoiding hyperventilation during BVM bagging (mean ventilation rate ~33/min vs target 10/min) and ensuring explicit closed-loop confirmation when considering adjunct medications such as sodium bicarbonate (04:06, 05:51).
redcap_row.general_comments_v2: Clear, calm leadership by the Team Leader with strong shared mental models, frequent thinking-out-loud reviews of H's and T's, and proactive input from the Compressor (suggesting lung auscultation at 03:12 and POC glucose at 04:08) — Specifically, role assignment was established at @01:02 (utt_002) and collaborative H's & T's input was solicited at @02:53 (utt_008), with verbal readback on Epinephrine #1 (@01:41–01:48) and bilateral breath sounds (@03:11–03:18). However, at @05:51 (utt_019), Sodium Bicarbonate was suggested ('We could do an amp of sodium bicarbonate') without a directed order to MED_RN or verbal administration readback (total_bicarb_v2 = 0), and a single compressor (CLIN-2) performed chest compressions continuously for 4m 48s (@01:20–06:08) without switching at the @03:49 rhythm check.
redcap_row.other_med_considered_list_v2: Sodium Bicarbonate (considered for acidosis at 04:06 and 05:51), IV Fluids (post-ROSC at 06:34)

So, this man is a 57, or this woman is a 57-year-old woman who has emphysema and is on oxygen at home. Her family states that the patient has been ill with nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea for several days. In the past 48 hours, she's been unable to eat or drink anything. Today she had more trouble breathing than usual, and her breathing has gradually worsened. She was found by EMS unresponsive and cyanotic at home. Um, we found her in a hospital-type bed, and she appeared to be non-responsive. We started CPR and we placed an IV. Um, her initial vitals: she had a heart rate of 116, respiratory rate of zero, there was no pulse, um, no oxygen, and her heart rhythm was sinus tachycardia with a PEA. Um, and yes, please assign yourself roles and begin.
Do I do compressions or airway? Okay, you can do compressions, I'll do airway.
Meds. I can be the provider. All right.
So, compressions. Start compressions.

So we knew she was in PEA when she came in. Um, we don't have an airway, so we want to get an airway. Um, she's currently in PEA still, so we can't shock. Um, we need to push one of epinephrine while we're getting the airway.
So I'm going to give meds, 1 milligram of epinephrine.
Okay, so one of epi's given. We have our airway. We're currently bagging. We're doing CPR. Um, airway's in.

Um, so we know that she was found unresponsive. She has a history of what, was it emphysema? Um, she wears oxygen at home, we know about. Um, she's in PEA, so we can rule out other things that we think's happening. Um, as far as like H's and T's, she could be hypoxic, um, she could have any type of like clot or thrombus with her, um, emphysema breathing history, like a PE. Um, I don't know if we got labs or anything else yet, like electrolytes. Does she have a cardiac history? Was there any cardiac stuff?
And she was having diarrhea before.

All right, so that makes sense for electrolyte derangements. Um, with the cardiac history, it could, you know, that could make a cardiac issue with electrolytes. Um, we know it's PEA, it's probably, we'll say two minutes, we can do a pulse check. We already pushed one of epinephrine. Um, is there any other suggestions?
Um, if we could listen to lung sounds to confirm placement.
All right, listening.
You hear bilateral breath sounds.
Okay, ET tube is in, we're bagging. Um, any other recommendations of other meds we can give, other than the epinephrine?
We can say it's about two minutes, so let's do a pulse check and see where our rhythm's at. Does she have a pulse?
You do not feel a pulse.
So continue compressions. She's still in PEA. Um, we can give another push of epinephrine.
Gave epinephrine.
Uh, we could give sodium bicarbonate.
Uh, can we get a point-of-care glucose? With a fingerstick.
We don't have labs back, but your point-of-care glucose is within normal range.

We could do like CBC, CMP, um, I would do a troponin, um, get a VBG and lactate, or just do an ABG and just see what her oxygen status was before, um, do a D-dimer, sounds like a possibility of a PE. If family's here, we can start getting a history from the family and talking to them.
No, family is not here.
How long was she down for?
Unknown downtime.

We could do an amp of sodium bicarbonate, I'm sure she's got like some acidosis going on. Um, it's about two minutes, we can check a pulse again. So we're going to do a pulse check. Do we have a pulse?
You guys have a pulse. Um, so now her repeat vitals are: she is tachycardic to 110, blood pressure is 95 over 77, respiratory rate 14, SpO2 is 94, and her pCO2 is 40.
So do we know what rhythm she's in? Normal sinus? Okay.
We can give fluids. She's dehydrated most likely, so, yeah.
Pulm, cardiology should be consulted. Um, we're still waiting for blood work. I would get an EKG now, CT head just to rule out strokes, or chest X-ray to confirm like the ET tube and everything.
All right guys, this ends your sim. Thank you.

done_well.title: Rapid recognition of non-shockable PEA and immediate Epinephrine administration
done_well.detail: Within 24 seconds of starting compressions (01:20), the Team Leader explicitly stated that PEA is non-shockable (01:24) and directed 1 mg IV Epinephrine, which was administered and confirmed at 01:44.
done_well.evidence_quote: She's currently in PEA still, so we can't shock. Um, we need to push one of epi while we're getting the airway.

done_well.category: Reversible Causes (H's & T's) & Team Mutual Support
done_well.title: Thorough H's & T's synthesis and proactive team cross-monitoring
done_well.detail: The Team Leader synthesized history (emphysema, home O2, severe diarrhea) into targeted H's and T's (hypoxia, pulmonary embolism, electrolyte disturbance/hypovolemia) at 02:00-02:55, while the Compressor proactively prompted bilateral lung auscultation (03:12) and point-of-care glucose testing (04:08).
done_well.evidence_quote: As far as like H's and T's, she could be hypoxic... clot or thrombus... And she was having diarrhea before -> electrolyte derangements.

areas_for_improvement.title: Avoid excessive BVM ventilation rate during CPR
areas_for_improvement.detail: Manikin airway sensors recorded 91 ventilations over the resuscitation (mean rate ~33.2 breaths/min), exceeding the AHA ACLS target of 10 breaths/min (1 breath every 6 seconds) with an advanced airway.
areas_for_improvement.actionable_recommendation: Once the LMA/advanced airway is in place, time squeezing the bag to 1 breath every 6 seconds (10 breaths/min) using the timer or counting 'one-one-thousand' to six to prevent increased intrathoracic pressure and reduced venous return.

areas_for_improvement.title: Convert tentative medication suggestions into explicit orders or deferrals
areas_for_improvement.detail: At 04:06 and 05:51, the Team Leader mentioned 'we could give bicarb / could do an amp of bicarb' for suspected acidosis, and earlier mentioned fluids during arrest, without issuing a direct order to the Med RN or receiving closed-loop confirmation.
areas_for_improvement.actionable_recommendation: When thinking out loud as Team Leader, clearly distinguish between differential discussion and active orders by addressing the Medication Nurse directly ('Give 1 amp of sodium bicarbonate IV now' or 'Hold off on bicarb until ABG returns').

engine_team_review.team_narrative: Clear, calm leadership by the Team Leader with strong shared mental models, frequent thinking-out-loud reviews of H's and T's, and proactive input from the Compressor (suggesting lung auscultation at 03:12 and POC glucose at 04:08) — Specifically, role assignment was established at @01:02 (utt_002) and collaborative H's & T's input was solicited at @02:53 (utt_008), with verbal readback on Epinephrine #1 (@01:41–01:48) and bilateral breath sounds (@03:11–03:18). However, at @05:51 (utt_019), Sodium Bicarbonate was suggested ('We could do an amp of sodium bicarbonate') without a directed order to MED_RN or verbal administration readback (total_bicarb_v2 = 0), and a single compressor (CLIN-2) performed chest compressions continuously for 4m 48s (@01:20–06:08) without switching at the @03:49 rhythm check.
engine_team_review.technical_narrative: Prompt ACLS PEA management: CPR started at 01:20 (18s after handoff), LMA placed at 01:31, 1st Epinephrine 1 mg IV given at 01:44, bilateral breath sounds confirmed at 03:24, 1st 2-min pulse check at 03:47 with minimal pause (<8s), 2nd Epinephrine 1 mg IV at 04:04, and ROSC achieved at 06:08.
engine_team_review.feedback_narrative: At 01:02, the team rapidly assigned roles (Compressor, Airway, Meds, Team Leader) and initiated chest compressions at 01:20. The Team Leader immediately recognized PEA as a non-shockable rhythm (01:24), prioritized airway placement (01:31) and Epinephrine 1 mg IV (administered at 01:44), and systematically verbalized H's and T's (hypoxia, PE/thrombus, hypovolemia/electrolyte derangement from diarrhea at 02:00-02:55). The Compressor proactively requested lung auscultation at 03:12 to confirm airway placement. Two-minute pulse checks were well-timed (03:47 and 06:00) with a second dose of Epinephrine at 04:04. Upon achieving ROSC at 06:08, the team appropriately ordered IV fluids, 12-lead ECG, chest X-ray, head CT, and specialist consultations. Areas for refinement include avoiding hyperventilation during BVM bagging (mean ventilation rate ~33/min vs target 10/min) and ensuring explicit closed-loop confirmation when considering adjunct medications such as sodium bicarbonate (04:06, 05:51).

done_well.title: Rapid recognition of non-shockable PEA and immediate Epinephrine administration
done_well.detail: Within 24 seconds of starting compressions (01:20), the Team Leader explicitly stated that PEA is non-shockable (01:24) and directed 1 mg IV Epinephrine, which was administered and confirmed at 01:44.
done_well.evidence_quote: She's currently in PEA still, so we can't shock. Um, we need to push one of epi while we're getting the airway.

done_well.category: Reversible Causes (H's & T's) & Team Mutual Support
done_well.title: Thorough H's & T's synthesis and proactive team cross-monitoring
done_well.detail: The Team Leader synthesized history (emphysema, home O2, severe diarrhea) into targeted H's and T's (hypoxia, pulmonary embolism, electrolyte disturbance/hypovolemia) at 02:00-02:55, while the Compressor proactively prompted bilateral lung auscultation (03:12) and point-of-care glucose testing (04:08).
done_well.evidence_quote: As far as like H's and T's, she could be hypoxic... clot or thrombus... And she was having diarrhea before -> electrolyte derangements.

areas_for_improvement.title: Avoid excessive BVM ventilation rate during CPR
areas_for_improvement.detail: Manikin airway sensors recorded 91 ventilations over the resuscitation (mean rate ~33.2 breaths/min), exceeding the AHA ACLS target of 10 breaths/min (1 breath every 6 seconds) with an advanced airway.
areas_for_improvement.actionable_recommendation: Once the LMA/advanced airway is in place, time squeezing the bag to 1 breath every 6 seconds (10 breaths/min) using the timer or counting 'one-one-thousand' to six to prevent increased intrathoracic pressure and reduced venous return.

areas_for_improvement.title: Convert tentative medication suggestions into explicit orders or deferrals
areas_for_improvement.detail: At 04:06 and 05:51, the Team Leader mentioned 'we could give bicarb / could do an amp of bicarb' for suspected acidosis, and earlier mentioned fluids during arrest, without issuing a direct order to the Med RN or receiving closed-loop confirmation.
areas_for_improvement.actionable_recommendation: When thinking out loud as Team Leader, clearly distinguish between differential discussion and active orders by addressing the Medication Nurse directly ('Give 1 amp of sodium bicarbonate IV now' or 'Hold off on bicarb until ABG returns').
areas_for_improvement.evidence_quote: We could do an amp of bicarb, I'm sure she's got like some acidosis going on.

engine_team_review.human_feedback_narrative: verbalized reversible causes of cardiac pea arrest, gave appropriate meds, no closed loop communication regarding admin of bicarb etc so I could not tell if it was actually given, appreciated leader asking for opinions, consider switching out for compressions and delegating differently
engine_team_review.human_team_comments: Could improve in closed loop communication particularly around administration of meds, it was not clear if certain meds were administered or not. They did do a good job of collaborating mentally, they had clear defined roles and were calm and organized.
